defect.title: Overwrite's new `TType extends object ? (TWith extends object ? merge : TWith)` branch replaces an object context with a nullable ctx override, so a middleware calling next({ ctx: X | undefined }) (or null/undefined) types downstream ctx as possibly undefined/null although the runtime always merges
defect.trigger: An object root context plus a middleware whose next() ctx argument is, or includes in a union, a non-object type: `next({ ctx: cond ? { a: 1 } : undefined })`, `next({ ctx: maybeExtra })` with `maybeExtra: X | undefined`, `next({ ctx: cond ? {...} : null })`, or `next({ ctx: undefined })`. A later resolver or middleware then reads ctx.
defect.consequence: At the head (published as @trpc/server 10.43.3), tsc rejects code that compiled at 10.43.2. The errors are TS18048 "'ctx' is possibly 'undefined'" and TS18047 "'ctx' is possibly 'null'". With a literal `next({ ctx: undefined })`, ctx is typed exactly `undefined`, and every property read fails. The runtime (procedureBuilder.ts:371-374, `{ ...callOpts.ctx, ...nextOpts.ctx }`) never produces an undefined or null ctx, so the types contradict the runtime and force spurious guards or casts.
defect.evidence: Scratch tsc 5.1.3 (clone's binary, --strict) over git-archive copies of packages/server/src at the merge-base, at the head, and at the head with de858987's utils.ts/types.ts. Base: no probe errors. Head: TS2322 on Overwrite<{a:1}, undefined> ('not assignable to type undefined'), and TS18048/TS18047 on conditional-undefined, literal-undefined, optional-variable, conditional-null and reusable t.middleware cases. Fix (#5039, shipped as 10.43.4 on 2023-11-17): no probe errors. The npm 10.43.3 dist/core/internals/utils.d.ts contains the head's gate. The 10.43.4 version switches to `TWith extends any ? TType extends object ? {merge} : TWith`. No downstream issue report was found.
defect.required_outcome: When the incoming context is an object type, a ctx override that is (or includes in a union) undefined, null or another non-object must not replace or widen the downstream context to that non-object type. For those members the downstream ctx must keep the incoming context's properties, matching the runtime spread-merge and the 10.43.2 typing. This must hold together with GT-j1's and GT-j2's required outcomes, and with #5020's primitive-input overwrite fix.
manifestations: TS18048 'ctx' is possibly 'undefined' after next({ ctx: cond ? {...} : undefined }) or next({ ctx: maybeUndefinedValue })
TS18047 'ctx' is possibly 'null' after next({ ctx: cond ? {...} : null })
ctx typed exactly undefined after next({ ctx: undefined })

rulings.reasoning: TRUE AT HEAD, NOT AT BASE: the claim reproduces. I type-checked scratch copies of packages/server/src (git archive main / review-head into clone-work/base and clone-work/head, plus a third tree 'fix' = head with de858987's utils.ts and types.ts swapped in) using the clone's tsc 5.1.3 with --strict. The same probe.ts was used in all three. At the merge-base, none of the probe lines has an error. At the head: "probe.ts(8,14): error TS2322: Type '{ a: number; }' is not assignable to type 'undefined'." (Overwrite<{a:1}, undefined>); "probe.ts(15,23): error TS18048: 'ctx' is possibly 'undefined'." (use(opts => opts.next({ ctx: cond ? { a: 1 } : undefined })).query(({ctx}) => ctx.user.id)); the same TS18048 for next({ ctx: undefined }) (line 30), for next({ ctx: extra }) with extra: {a:number}|undefined (line 36), and for a reusable t.middleware (line 45); and "probe.ts(41,23): error TS18047: 'ctx' is possibly 'null'." for cond ? {a:1} : null. In a sanity probe for literal next({ ctx: undefined }), ctx becomes exactly undefined at the head: "TS2339: Property 'user' does not exist on type 'never'" after ctx!. At the base and at the fix, the same line yields the expected "Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'string'", so ctx is typed, not any. The 6 errors inside packages/server (TS7017/TS2591, from environment typing) are the same in all trees. The #5039 fix tree has no probe errors. MECHANISM / INTRODUCED BY THIS PR: the PR adds the branch `TType extends object ? (TWith extends object ? merge : TWith extends any ? TWith : never)`. When TWith is `X | undefined`, the branch distributes, so the undefined member replaces the whole object context. At the base, `TType extends any ? TWith extends any ? {mapped over keyof TType | keyof TWith}` maps undefined to TType's own keys. MiddlewareFunction's next is `<$Context>(opts: { ctx: $Context })`, which is unconstrained, so undefined/null are accepted API inputs. At runtime, procedureBuilder.ts:371-374 always merges `{ ...callOpts.ctx, ...nextOpts.ctx }`, so the runtime ctx is never undefined or null. The type therefore contradicts the runtime. UPSTREAM: the published @trpc/server 10.43.3 (npm 2023-11-10T10:19Z) ships this exact Overwrite. 10.43.4 (2023-11-17T12:32Z, containing #5039/de858987) changes it to `TWith extends any ? TType extends object ? {merge} : TWith : never`, which maps an undefined TWith back to TType's keys. v10.45.2 keeps that shape. I confirmed with tsc that the fix tree removes every probe error. So upstream's final semantics restored 10.43.2 behaviour for this case. NOT IN REGISTER: GT-j1 concerns unconstrained generic type parameters in middleware factories dropping ctx/input properties. Its required outcome (no prototype-key iteration for primitive/primitive; generic-derived params do not drop properties) does not cover a concrete nullable TWith replacing an object TType. #5039's own prose ('check whether TWith extends a JS primitive, and if so, wholly replaces it') describes a GT-j1-sufficient design that would keep this behaviour, because undefined is a primitive. GT-j2 concerns TType = any taking both branches, which is a different operand and mechanism. No non_defect covers it: the index-signature, redundancy, dead-code, performance and test-coverage entries are all unrelated. MATERIAL: this is a type-level compatibility break in a patch release. Code that compiles at 10.43.2 fails tsc at 10.43.3, and the break is demonstrated by my reproduction at base, head and fix. The resulting type is also unsound relative to runtime, since ctx is typed possibly undefined/null when it never is. This is the same kind of evidence and bar on which GT-j2 was admitted. COUNTER-ARGUMENTS: (1) Passing a nullable ctx to next() is unidiomatic. No in-repo test or example does it (a Grep for next({ ctx: ...?/&&/undefined/null over the clone found no matches). GitHub issue search found no downstream report ('possibly undefined' ctx: 0 results; the only 10.43.3 reports are #5037 (GT-j1), #5042 and #5075, which are unrelated). The consequence could therefore be called hypothetical. I do not accept this as decisive. The API signature explicitly admits the input; `session && { user }`-style and optional-value forwarding idioms produce exactly these unions; the break is deterministic; and the release lived only 7 days before 10.43.4 changed the behaviour, which explains the missing reports. The lack of a report lowers the priority, not the truth of the claim. (2) The PR's doc comment says 'Otherwise it will overwrite the entire TType with TWith', so the behaviour could be called intended. For input overwrite that is right, but Overwrite is also the ctx combinator (middleware.ts:65,103,136; procedureBuilder.ts:38), where the runtime merges rather than replaces. Upstream reversed this for object TType in 10.43.4. I rule material, with lower severity than GT-j1.
